reason: The plan is invalid because it fundamentally misunderstands the hypothesis. The hypothesis concerns the VC dimension of the network class (approximation capacity for zero violation), but the plan proposes measuring generalization error on a held-out set with a fixed 'rigid' analytical function family. This tests approximation error/generalization, not the theoretical lower bound on width required for zero violation. To test the hypothesis, one must vary the constraint system (not just sample size w) and find the minimal width where zero violation is achievable across constraint configurations, not just for a single function.
missing_steps: Reframe hypothesis testing from generalization error to zero-violation feasibility across constraint systems
Generate diverse constraint systems (not just samples from one function) to test solvability
Measure N_c(w) as minimal width achieving zero violation across constraint configurations, not minimal width for small held-out error
Compare against VC dimension scaling O(d h log h) by varying d, h, and constraint counts systematically
